perspective:
From Harold Padilla’s perspective, he has access to:

- He is Harold Padilla, a project manager. He feels frustrated and anxious that his project is behind and believes his team is unmotivated, which is hurting progress.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend/professional contact he relies on for advice and support.
- He arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur. He heard Arthur advise that motivation is tricky, that he should understand each team member’s individual drivers, and that one-on-one conversations can help because people need to feel valued and understood.
- Harold told Arthur he had been focused on goals and deadlines rather than personal motivations. He said he would try Arthur’s suggestion and felt more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold felt hopeful and relieved. He told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. He heard Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each person and wanted to make the project a success together.
- Later, Harold noticed the team still was not responding well. He felt disappointed and worried and told Arthur this.
- He heard Arthur say there may be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper. Harold said he had not thought of that, would set up more meetings, and thanked Arthur.
- Harold became determined and focused, believing there might be unaddressed underlying team issues. He held one-on-one meetings and asked team members to share concerns or problems.
- He heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few people affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts and redistribute tasks to ease pressure, and that their well-being mattered.
- Harold felt optimistic and empowered, believing that addressing individual concerns would improve team performance. He decided to create a more supportive, open environment with regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- He told the team about these changes. He heard Team Member 1 say it sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold said he was glad and that their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

He does not have access to hidden events, other characters’ private thoughts, or narrator-only information beyond what he observed, heard, was told, or did himself.
